lineage: Provenance: this package FORKS the accepted lead 0a45ddb2 (116.793080), whose own lineage is cbadde77 -> 6ecec8e3 -> cf6d45a8 -> 0a45ddb2; all four are declared as dependencies. Every identity, size, itemisation, bound, cap, price and toy result is restated and re-verified in THIS package; nothing is inherited by citation. This revision (v6) answers the v5 review's surviving accounting objections with implementation analyses, not assertions: (1) the field inversion is priced by its algorithm - binary extended Euclid on 381-bit six-limb values, at most 762 conditional subtract/shift steps at 18 limb operations each = 13,716 instructions, charged 2^14 = 16,384 (the v5 figure of 3830 had no derivation); the gap-table build accordingly charges (2000 + 16384 + 47)/2000 = 9.22 reference additions per entry, 2^100.20; (2) the square root is priced by Tonelli-Shanks at v2(r-1) = 32: the odd-part exponentiation (~310 F_r-multiplications at 4-bit windows) plus at most 32 correction rounds each of at most 34 F_r-multiplications = at most ~1400, charged 2048 (the v5 figure of 512 counted neither the odd part nor the correction rounds correctly); (3) the point scalar multiplication is priced by the projective 4-bit fixed-window method: at most 330 point operations over all k < r, run in projective coordinates (~11 F_r-multiplications each, no inversions) plus ONE final inversion = 1,405,213 instructions = 702.6 reference additions, charged 704 - sequential scalar multiplications cannot batch inversions, and the v5 charge of 383 reference additions priced only the point operations without their field cost; (4) the base-prime search closes with a supply bound: the interval [2^80, 2^80 + 2^91.98] is sized at the FAR-END density (ln ~ 63.2 at q ~ 2^91) for an EXPECTED 2^66 H-primes against the 2^65 requirement, and the shortfall is the new cap C9, a Chernoff tail 2^-1.3e19 at delta = 1/2 (the v5 interval used the near-2^80 density over a 2^90.79-long span, which cannot hold). The standing fork changes against the lead remain: K = 51/100 (jungjipdo's own margin) and the per-record charge 160 over the 33-line six-limb itemisation (listing 129/122, a 24 percent margin, against the lead's 26 percent over 143 at 180). Net: W = 141261532748131723019091876932305269 units, score 116.765852, a gain of 0.027228 bits on the accepted lead.
work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = records + per-node fixed work + comparisons + gap tables + candidate re-walk (including both table rebuilds) + strand starts + segment starts + status tree + base H-primes + walk list + split gaps + candidate multiplications + kept blocks + candidate copy + Lemma 1, with records = 2N x 2000 x (1 + 160/2000), N = 65196422678611482903494932429799424 = 2^64 x L per side (L = 3534305155321689 steps, all w distinct), m = (r-1)/2^20, K = 51/100; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. W(2^20) = 141261532748131723019091876932305269 units exactly. Score = ceil(10^6 log2 W)/10^6 = 116.765852 = 116765852/1000000.
heuristics: H1 (coverage; the load-bearing heuristic): the 6N^2(1 - (L-1)/L^2) independent rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z = s^d like uniform elements of the order-m subgroup H, so the success probability is at least 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39950 at the lower bound K = 0.51 (the realised 6N^2/m is 0.51 x (1 + 2^-54.2)). Support: Lemma 4 (the six-fold symmetry and the parity key make the six orbit images of one record share one key and one comparison), the L-entry walk list giving exactly N = 2^64 x L distinct scalars per side, the diagonal collapse K' = K(1 - (L-1)/L^2), the three coverage toys (d = 32/64/128 at r ~ 2^27.6/2^29.7/2^31.7, measured 0.4167/0.4333/0.3333 against predicted 0.3974/0.3913/0.3974, z = +0.43/+0.94/-1.43) and the end-to-end toy (measured 0.3833 against 0.3935 predicted, z = -0.23).

H2 and H2' (supply): a fraction 1/2^20 of primes near q are H-primes (q^m = 1 mod r); gaps between consecutive H-primes are exponential with mean 2^20 ln q, so the L-th (L = 2^51.6503) H-prime above 2^39 is below 2^78 and a gap above 2^33 among the listed ones has probability < 2^-167 per list (such gaps split into two table entries against the reserve). The base-prime search interval is sized at the FAR-END density for an expected 2^66 H-primes against the 2^65 requirement, the shortfall a Chernoff tail (C9). Checked by the run's H-prime sanity block: 402 of the 6542 primes below 2^16 are sixteenth powers against 408.875 expected (binomial z = -0.34).

H3 (key bits): the 192-bit parity-selected y keys of the walked points behave like independent uniform strings across the six-element mu_6 orbits. This is a heuristic about coordinates of structured points; the end-to-end toy bins 16-bit truncated keys into 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads and reports occupancy chi^2 = 24.27 on 31 degrees of freedom (z = -0.85).

Caps C1-C9 (ours, every tail rounded towards the larger probability): C1 comparisons per node (Bernstein, 2^-94845 over all nodes); C2 head-slot depth (Poisson 0.392, tail 2^-82.6 over 2^117 slots); C3 node record-count deviations (Chernoff 2^-3008); C4 false candidate pairs - a compared pair already agrees on the 84 routing and 33 slot key bits, so false matches cost 2^-75 per comparison, expected N^2/2^192 = 2^39.30, cap 2^44 with Chernoff tail (e mu/t)^t = 2^-5.7e13; C5 true matches, two channels - off-diagonal Poisson(0.51) tail exp(-1.42e7) = 2^-2.0e7 at the 2^20 cap, and the diagonal challenges z = a/a' which abort at the caps with union probability 6*2^128/m = 2^-104.27 (the same single event that would break C4 and C7); C6 candidate sinks (owner lists: per-node mean 2^-44.7 against 2^16 slots, tail 2^-3.9e6; generating-node kept blocks: mean 2^20.30 against 2^24 slots, tail 2^-3.8e7); C7 re-walk key repeats - the retained key already occurs, so >= 5 kept steps need 4 further hits at 2^-192 each, L^5/(5!*2^768) per chain, 2^-451.7 over all chains; C8 node overflow against the pool capacity ceil(2^33.32) linked records (Chernoff 2^-1309819329 plus a 2^-20 modelling budget); C9 base-prime supply shortfall below the 2^65 requirement at expected supply 2^66 (Chernoff 2^-1.3e19). Success claimed = 0.39950 - 2^-40 (every cap tail, C1-C9) - 2^-20 (C8 modelling) = 0.395 >= 0.39.
limitations: This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.
H1 and H3 are validated at toy scale only (the three coverage toys and the end-to-end run in this package's own evidence).

Instruction counts are itemised analytic counts from an AArch64-scalar-style listing at six 64-bit limbs per field element, not hardware measurements; every shared price (the F_r-multiplication at 383, the inversion at 2^14 by binary extended Euclid, the projective 4-bit-window scalar multiplication at 704, the Tonelli-Shanks square root at 2048, the modexp at 512) is derived as a worst-case bound in proof.md section 3 with its algorithm, and the cluster model is the accepted lineage's definition restated.

Memory is exponential, as for any BSGS-form Cheon attack: the exact integer sum is 2^122.806 bytes (the retained 2^32 x 96-byte gap table per generating node and the 40-byte linked pool records included), claimed at its ceiling 2^122.81.

The per-record charge 160 is an itemised analytic count over a 33-line six-limb listing whose maximal variant is 129/122; it is not a hardware measurement. The score sits 0.0272 bits under the accepted lead; the gain is the lead's own published slack (K 0.51, charge 180->160 at comparable 24/26 percent margins) net of the honest repricing this package adds; a reviewer who prices any line differently gets a different number and the ledger is a single script.
